name: Explanation unclear

title: "[Unclear] "
labels: ["documentation", "explanation-unclear"]
assignees: []
---

<!--
Thank you for telling us! Confusing explanations are one of the most valuable things to report,
because fixing them helps every learner who comes after you.

You do NOT need to know the answer or suggest a fix. "I got lost here" is a perfectly good report.
Nothing here is a silly question.

If something is actually wrong (a math mistake or code that gives a wrong result),
please use the "Bug report" template instead.
-->

## Which lesson is this about?

<!-- File path or link, plus the section heading. Example: `curriculum/07-eigenvalues-eigenvectors/1-intuition.md`, "Why eigenvectors don't change direction" -->

- **Unit / file:**
- **Section or heading:**
- **Link (optional):**

## What kind of problem is it?

<!-- Tick everything that applies. -->

- [ ] A term or symbol is used before it is defined
- [ ] A step in a derivation or proof is skipped
- [ ] The intuition or picture doesn't match the formulas
- [ ] The example is too hard, too abstract, or too short
- [ ] The code is hard to follow, or I can't tell what it does
- [ ] The visualization is unclear or missing labels
- [ ] An exercise is ambiguous or its solution doesn't explain the reasoning
- [ ] The prerequisites are missing or the lesson assumes too much
- [ ] The order of topics feels wrong
- [ ] Other

## What confused you?

<!--
Quote or point to the exact sentence, equation, or line of code where you got stuck, and say what you
were expecting or what you didn't understand. The more specific, the better.
-->

## What did you already understand?

<!--
Optional but very helpful. Where did it still make sense? This shows where the explanation stops
working for you. Example: "I understand what a matrix times a vector does, but I got lost when
the lesson started talking about the null space."
-->

## About you (optional)

<!-- This helps us pitch explanations at the right level. Share only what you're comfortable with. -->

- **Your background with linear algebra:** brand new / some exposure (school or a first course) / comfortable
- **Programming experience:** none / some Python / confident in Python
- **What you're using this for:** self-study / a university course / machine learning / robotics / other

## Suggestion (optional)

<!--
If you have an idea, share it, for example a picture, an analogy, a worked example, a link to an
explanation that clicked for you, or a rewrite of the confusing sentence. If not, leave this blank.
-->

## Additional context

<!-- Anything else that might help. Screenshots are welcome. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] I read the section more than once before reporting
- [ ] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate
- [ ] I'm happy to be asked a follow-up question about what was unclear
